profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting between two engineers on a compiler-fuzzing infrastructure team after a nightly benchmark regression appears in their new test-case reducer. The team recently added hoisting to their Hierarchical Delta Debugging (HDD) implementation for JavaScript ASTs, and the nightly dashboard now shows that some reduced test cases are larger than expected, while one well-known crash case no longer seems to reproduce consistently for developers. The meeting context is an urgent 30-minute sync before deciding whether to keep hoisting enabled in the nightly pipeline. The agenda is to compare what each person observed, narrow down whether the issue is in the hoisting logic, the benchmark harness, or the cached reducer state, and agree on the immediate next debugging step. The expected outcome is a shared plan for a targeted rerun and a likely root-cause hypothesis, not a full fix during the meeting.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.expertise: AST-based reduction algorithms, grammar-aware test-case minimization, reducer implementation details
members.background: Priya built the team's original HDD reducer for tree-structured fuzz inputs and recently implemented the hoisting extension in the JavaScript reduction service.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid rolling back hoisting before an internal demo, suspects the nightly harness is amplifying a setup issue rather than exposing a core algorithm flaw, and is especially concerned about preserving bug-specific reproductions that help compiler engineers debug quickly.
hidden_assumptions: "Still failing" means the reduced test case triggers the same sanitizer stack fingerprint as the original crash, not just any failing exit.
"The js-487 case" refers to the frozen Jira repro artifact attached when she implemented hoisting, because that is the canonical version she has been using locally.
If the grammar bundle changes, the compatibility and parse caches are automatically invalidated, because her local benchmark script always rebuilds them.
"Baseline HDD" means the current main-branch reducer with the newer pretty-printer and node-count objective, since that is what she compares against during development.
"Fixed" means hoisting remains enabled and produces a deterministic same-bug reproducer on representative cases, even if the suite-level dashboard has not fully stabilized yet.

members.name: Mateo Ruiz
members.expertise: CI benchmark orchestration, fuzzing triage, reproducibility workflows, nightly infrastructure
members.background: Mateo maintains the nightly reducer benchmark harness, corpus refresh jobs, and dashboard alerts used by the compiler and testing teams.
members.private_state: He wants to stop the nightly instability with minimal reruns, is wary of expensive full-suite debugging, and mainly cares that the pipeline returns to predictable benchmark behavior by tomorrow morning.
hidden_assumptions: "Still failing" means the target program still trips the oracle wrapper with a non-zero exit, timeout, or crash, regardless of whether it is the exact same crash family.
"The js-487 case" refers to the current nightly corpus item under that stable corpus ID, even if the underlying seed was regenerated during the weekend corpus refresh.
Cache reuse is safe across grammar-bundle updates unless the AST schema version changes, so the nightly workers can keep warm compatibility data.
"Baseline HDD" means the reproducibility branch used for the last published benchmark comparison, which still measures output size in bytes after formatting.
"Fixed" means the nightly dashboard no longer shows a practical regression in runtime or output size at the suite level, even if one specific bug fingerprint changes.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the reduced test case should 'still fail' or 'still reproduce'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the reduced output must trigger the same AddressSanitizer crash signature and stack fingerprint as the original failing test.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the reduced output only needs to make the oracle wrapper report failure somehow, including timeout, generic non-zero exit, or a different crash.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In reducer discussions, 'still fails' is routine shorthand, and both participants assume the oracle interpretation is already shared because the harness has been stable for months.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'js-487' and 'the splice crash case' as though it were one fixed benchmark input.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the frozen Jira attachment from two weeks ago that she used for local development and manual repro checks.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the current nightly corpus artifact with the same corpus ID after an automated corpus refresh regenerated the underlying seed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Stable corpus IDs create a strong sense of sameness, and neither expects that a benchmark item with the same label could now point to a different concrete input file.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about using 'the same container' or 'the same setup' when comparing local and nightly reducer behavior.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes that cache invalidation for parse trees and compatibility maps is part of the normal setup whenever the grammar bundle changes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes that cache lifecycle is independent from 'setup' unless there is an explicit parser-schema bump, so warm caches can persist across those runs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Container image identity usually stands in for environmental equivalence, so neither participant initially thinks to unpack cache invalidation rules as a separate dimension.

misalignment_points.topic: What it would mean for the issue to be 'fixed'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss getting the regression 'fixed' before the next nightly run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks it is fixed if hoisting produces deterministic same-bug reductions on the representative crash cases she cares about, even if aggregate dashboard numbers remain noisy.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks it is fixed if suite-level size and runtime regressions disappear from the dashboard, even if some individual reduced outputs now represent different failure fingerprints.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They both naturally aim for a 'fix' under time pressure, and the term sounds operationally aligned even though one is optimizing bug-faithfulness while the other is optimizing pipeline stability.
